findings.claim: The revised ownership scheme fixes the demonstrated round-1 counterexample, but item 5 overstates what the caller guards prove. Refusing begin while a target exists does not alone prove that every subsequent begin occurs after the preceding ended notification: ended is emitted at function exit, and dragEnd can synchronously reenter callbacks. If a callback can start a new session before that notification, an old ended could invalidate new ownership; similarly, a non-null target after begin does not by itself identify the session surviving reentrant execution. No such start path is demonstrated in the supplied Kwinish callbacks, so this is a conditional ordering concern, not an established failure or a reason to reject this preparation. Record the no-reentrant-start invariant and ensure unload callbacks cannot synchronously restart a drag, in addition to not scheduling deferred work.
findings.evidence: "Como todo fim de sessão com alvo passa por dragEnd e emite ended (scope guard)"; "Reentrada síncrona é possível"; "todos os beginDragTarget do host exigem ausência de alvo antes"; "Logo, uma nova sessão só começa depois de um ended".

findings.claim: The inventory still omits two explicit routing changes: the new Hotkeys interception branch, and forwarding captured button events to the keybind manager with captured=true instead of returning immediately. These are real source differences, but their observable consequences for Kwinish are not established here. In particular, captured=true explicitly bypasses the normal automatic drag-end call; do not describe every forwarded button event as ending a drag. Document these branches as investigated routing differences, with a capture/hotkey test if those configurations are supported, rather than asserting a new contractual failure.
findings.evidence: U adds "if (Hotkeys::mgr()->onButton(e, mouse))" followed by "Keybinds::mgr()->onMouseEvent(e, mouse, PROTO::inputCapture->isCaptured())"; its capture branch calls "Keybinds::mgr()->onMouseEvent(e, mouse, true)". O instead has "if (PROTO::inputCapture->isCaptured()) return;". U computes "const bool DRAG_WAS_ACTIVE = captured ? false : g_layoutManager->endDragTarget();".

notes:
Approval is for investigation, probes and documentation only. The material consistently reports no keybind, hook or lifecycle integration. The round-1 demonstrated ownership bug and incorrect no-reentry argument have been addressed. The remaining conditional ordering concern should accompany the separately authorized Q4 implementation, not be mistaken for a demonstrated current failure.

Row-by-row assessment:

K1: Correct replacement composition for the supplied call sites: existing-target guard, cursor hit-test with the same flags, fullscreen/decorations check, then beginDragTarget with the documented defaults. The probe helper's bool is not SDispatchResult, but every current caller ignores the result, so that difference is immaterial here. MAPDRAGHOTSPOT supports the proportional pickup change; it affects fullscreen as well as tiled windows, which sections 2 and 6 already acknowledge. Floating movement equivalence follows from the stated hotspot algebra. RD is appropriate; owner acceptance is still pending. Focusing the bar window does not change the cursor-based target selection.

K2: The resize candidate, arguments and ignored result are correct. Cursor-based selection rather than selection of the addressed window is inherited, not a port regression. RD accurately identifies an inherited observable hazard; the backend resizing implementation change is DI on the supplied evidence, not a demonstrated client-visible change. Using the addressed window directly would be a separate semantic decision.

K3: The guarded endDragTarget call is correct. Its bool can be ignored. Ending any active drag is inherited behavior, so DI is appropriate for the replacement itself. The decoration, grouping, geometry and focus effects in section 2 still apply; DI does not mean that ending a drag has no observable effects. This unconditional replacement must not be confused with the ownership-sensitive unload operation.

K4: floatWindow(TOGGLE_ACTION_ENABLE), with the default focused-window selection, matches the supplied legacy translation and documented activewindow equivalence. ActionResult is correct. The changed end helper does not establish a behavioral regression. DI is justified.

K5: Focused-window selection, a no-window guard, the same parser against GOAL size, the invalid-size guard, and resize(SIZ, false, W) reproduce the translator. ActionResult and Vector2D are correct. DI is justified. This is a wrapper to reproduce, not merely an opportunity to pass the bar's window directly.

K6: pinWindow(TOGGLE_ACTION_TOGGLE) on the focused window matches the translator and returns ActionResult. State storage and scheduling changes do not independently establish a contract-visible difference. DI is supported, with the proposed workspace-during-touch-drag test.

K7: Parsing against GOAL position and move(POS, false, W) match the translator. Preserve focused-window selection and its no-window guard for this operation as well; W must not accidentally become a cached bar window or a stale selection from initial touch setup. The explicit integer-cast requirement correctly prevents a fractional-coordinate change. DI is otherwise supported.

K8: floatWindow(TOGGLE_ACTION_DISABLE) is the correct settiled translation, with the same focused-window and ActionResult considerations as K4. DI is supported.

K9: The leading 0 was discarded by mouseDispatcher; it was not an independent release flag. Given the documented outside-bind m_passPressed == -1 premise, guarded endDragTarget reproduces the old effect. The possible m_passPressed == 1 reentrant case is explicitly identified as a hypothesis, not demonstrated. DI is reasonable under that premise.

K10: The translator explicitly maps argument 1 to MAXIMIZED and argument 0 here to FULLSCREEN, supplying true for toggling. The proposed overload and ActionResult are correct. DI is supported by the reported unchanged action body.

K11: The string overload with silent=true and default focused-window selection is the appropriate candidate and returns ActionResult. Workspace resolution/readiness, changed fallback focus, and pointer-constraint suspension are correctly distinguished from compile-time shape checking. Changed fallback focus is RD under the owner's stated contract. The new window->m_workspace != POLDWS guard is also visible in the diff; a changed outcome requires a case where the move does not actually change workspace, which is not established for this minimize call. Verify special:minimized naming and no-follow behavior at runtime; neither a successful compile nor the RD classification proves those contractual properties.

K12: Direct spawn(cmd) preserves the operation performed by the legacy wrapper and returns optional<uint64_t>. The wrapper's failure conversion was ignored by these callers, so discarding the optional preserves their existing error-handling policy. DI is supported.

K13: The revision correctly separates removal of name lookup from action failures and diagnostic policy. Existing ActionResult failures were already wrapped and discarded; spawn has a different result type. Direct typed calls are appropriate for this fixed known operation set. DI is supported. Logging previously discarded failures remains a separate choice.

Section 2: The old changeMouseBindMode reconstruction and candidate are accurate for these uses. exclusiveDeviceGrab already existed; keeping false preserves the plugin's behavior. Neither that accessor nor dragEnd's bool establishes ownership. The bool reports that an initial target existed, including early-return paths, not successful completion of all geometry/focus work. Empty end returns before constructing the ended scope guard and does not emit ended. The added m_draggingTiled reset and per-(button, pointer) release tracking now address the round-1 omissions. A changed group-drop result remains a test candidate, not an established BC.

Q4: In ordinary serialized execution, the ended listener clears ownership before a later user-bind drag on the same live target, fixing the concrete previous defect. Skipping acquisition on helper early returns prevents adopting an already active user drag. Checking target after an actual begin handles a rejected begin that leaves no active target; there is then no active plugin drag to miss. Every accepted rearm, unsnap restart and luaGrab start must use the acquisition path, and the listener must already be installed before those starts. A proper weak pointer does not identify a new allocation merely because its address is reused, although the WP implementation is not supplied; target comparison is now only a secondary defense. The remaining reentrant ordering limitation is described in the finding. Synchronous calls back into the mapped module during unload are explicitly acknowledged. No callback after unmap is proved safe here, and the revised document correctly leaves that proof to Q3 and requires listener removal and deferred-work suppression.

Probe K: Non-vacuous. It checks real installed-header expressions, exact member signatures, selected action signatures, abbreviated calls, return types, enum values, callable legacy API absence, the ended signal/listen types, and candidate composition. The negative cases and mutation results support those compile-time checks within the reported runner's scope. BeginWithDefaults tests two-argument well-formedness, not default values. The m_passPressed assertion tests its type, not whether mouse reads it. Signal/listener type checks do not test delivery timing, ownership invalidation or disconnection safety. The revised text substantially respects those limits. The abbreviated moveToWorkspace probe uses an explicit std::string rather than the matrix's literal spelling; it demonstrates the intended two-argument string-overload call, not literally every expression spelling in the matrix. No runtime drag acquisition, focus, workspace name, or unload property follows from the probe.

No BC identified: justified as the qualified investigation conclusion, given the supplied account of the reviewed contractual sources. CONFIGURAVEL.md coverage is now recorded. No supplied evidence demonstrates a written-requirement violation. This is not proof of completed runtime equivalence: special:minimized/no-follow and grab behavior still require verification, and RD items still require tests and explicit owner acceptance. The separately approved P6 logging work does not need reopening on this evidence.
